# Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.TaskPool

> `TaskPoolJobFactory`, the simplest `IJobFactory`: every job it creates runs its delegate on the thread pool the moment `Start()` is called - no queue, no ordering, no concurrency limit, no scheduler to start or stop. The four job classes it produces (`TaskPoolJob`, `TaskPoolJobWithResult<TResult>`, `TaskPoolJobWithProgress<TProgress>`, `TaskPoolJobWithProgressAndResult<TProgress, TResult>`) are public and derive from the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Core` base classes. `Start()` validates and marks the job pending synchronously, then yields to the pool; the delegate's outcome becomes `IsCompletedSuccessfully`, `IsFaulted` with `Exception`, or `IsCanceled` when it honors the job's token. Targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.TaskPool`. All types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs` namespace - not `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.TaskPool`. Types:

- `TaskPoolJobFactory : IJobFactory` - parameterless constructor; eight virtual `Create` overloads returning `IJob`, `IJobWithResult<TResult>`, `IJobWithProgress<TProgress>`, `IJobWithProgressAndResult<TProgress, TResult>`
- `TaskPoolJob : Job`, `TaskPoolJobWithResult<TResult>`, `TaskPoolJobWithProgress<TProgress>`, `TaskPoolJobWithProgressAndResult<TProgress, TResult>` - public, not sealed; one constructor each taking the cancellable delegate shape (`Func<CancellationToken, Task>`, `Func<CancellationToken, Task<TResult>>`, `Func<IProgress<TProgress>, CancellationToken, Task>`, `Func<IProgress<TProgress>, CancellationToken, Task<TResult>>`); `override void Start()`

`Start()` guards and marks pending synchronously (a second call throws `InvalidOperationException` to the caller), then yields to the pool and runs the delegate there. Return means succeeded; `OperationCanceledException` after `Cancel()` means canceled; anything else means faulted with the original exception. The token-less `Create` overloads discard the token, so those jobs cannot be canceled. Progress reports are delivered asynchronously, possibly out of order and after completion. Nothing orders or limits jobs; use `Josupeit.Practices.Jobs.Scheduler` for that.
